title: Under the Hood: the low-owned players creating chances without the returns
dek: Thiago has 3.29 expected involvements and 1 to show for it, on 8.9% ownership. The gap between process and result is where differentials are found.
body:
## The gap between chances and goals

Expected goal involvements measure the positions a player gets into. Goals and assists measure what came of them. When the first runs well ahead of the second, one of two things is true: the player has been unlucky, or he is not good enough to finish what he creates. Over a long enough run it is almost always the first, which is why the gap is worth buying before it closes rather than after.

:::takeaways
- **Thiago** (8.9% owned) has 3.29 expected involvements and 1 actual.
- Every player here is under 10% owned — the gap is only worth anything while the field has not noticed.
- Based on 5 gameweeks of data. Treat it as a watchlist, not a shopping list.
:::

## Creating without converting

| Player | Team | Pos | Price | Owned | xGI | G+A | Waiting on | Mins |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Thiago** | BRE | FWD | £7.8m | 8.9% | 3.29 | 1 | **2.29** | 442 |
| **Barry** | EVE | FWD | £5.6m | 7.9% | 3.12 | 1 | **2.12** | 327 |
| **E.Le Fée** | SUN | MID | £5.8m | 3.5% | 2.88 | 1 | **1.88** | 348 |
| **Bobb** | FUL | MID | £5.5m | 0.3% | 1.37 | 0 | **1.37** | 273 |
| **Silva** | BOU | DEF | £5.0m | 0.4% | 1.12 | 0 | **1.12** | 360 |
| **McAtee** | NFO | MID | £5.5m | 0.1% | 1.08 | 0 | **1.08** | 334 |
| **Iwobi** | FUL | MID | £5.4m | 0.7% | 1.01 | 0 | **1.01** | 338 |
| **Buendía** | AVL | MID | £5.9m | 0.9% | 0.95 | 0 | **0.95** | 311 |

### How to read this table

The "waiting on" column is expected involvements minus actual returns. A figure of 1.0 means a player has generated the chances for one more goal or assist than he has produced. It is not a promise that the goal is coming — it is a statement that the chances are being created, which is the part of the process a player controls. Finishing regresses toward the mean over a season; getting into the box does not.

Ownership matters here as much as the gap. A player at 30% ownership whose returns are lagging is a hold, not a buy — you already have him, and so does everybody you are competing with. The same profile at 4% is a genuine edge, because you capture the correction and most of the field does not.

## Where the gap is concentrated

The same analysis by position, because the correction is worth different amounts depending on where a player lines up. An unconverted chance is worth six points to a defender and four to a forward, and defenders carry clean-sheet points on top.

| Position | Players under 10% owned | Average gap | Widest gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| **DEF** | 59 | 0.04 | Silva (1.12) |
| **MID** | 61 | -0.08 | E.Le Fée (1.88) |
| **FWD** | 11 | -0.01 | Thiago (2.29) |

## Taking more than they create

The mirror image, and the more dangerous group to own. These players have converted above the rate their chances imply. That is not an accusation — finishing is a real skill — but a player whose returns exceed his underlying numbers is priced on the returns, and the underlying numbers are what continue.

| Player | Team | Price | Owned | xGI | G+A | Above expectation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Schade | BRE | £6.1m | 7.7% | 1.84 | 5 | **+3.16** |
| Kamada | CRY | £5.0m | 0.5% | 0.4 | 3 | **+2.6** |
| Belloumi | HUL | £5.1m | 4.3% | 0.49 | 3 | **+2.51** |
| Davis | IPS | £4.0m | 6.8% | 1.61 | 4 | **+2.39** |
| Scott | BOU | £6.1m | 5.8% | 0.87 | 3 | **+2.13** |
| Evanilson | BOU | £6.0m | 3.2% | 1.22 | 3 | **+1.78** |

**Schade** has returned 3.16 more than his chances imply. That is not a sell signal on its own — a player who keeps getting into good positions will keep scoring even after the finishing cools — but it does mean the price you are paying reflects the best case rather than the underlying case.

## The minutes question

Every name above is only worth anything if he keeps starting. A player creating chances from sixty minutes a week is a different proposition to one doing it from ninety, and the low ownership that makes these players interesting is often low precisely because their place is not secure.

| Player | Team | Minutes | Mins per GW | Starts | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Thiago** | BRE | 442 | 88 | 5 | Fit |
| **Barry** | EVE | 327 | 65 | 4 | Fit |
| **E.Le Fée** | SUN | 348 | 70 | 4 | Fit |
| **Bobb** | FUL | 273 | 55 | 4 | Fit |
| **Silva** | BOU | 360 | 72 | 4 | Fit |
| **McAtee** | NFO | 334 | 67 | 4 | Fit |

1 of these 8 are playing 80 minutes or more a gameweek. Those are the ones where the gap between chances and returns is a genuine buying opportunity; the rest are watchlist entries whose first requirement is a run in the side.

:::callout data
Expected goals is a model, not a measurement. It assigns every shot the conversion rate of an average player from that position, which systematically undersells elite finishers and oversells poor ones. Read the gap as a question worth asking, not an answer.
:::
